sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned official documentation reopened 2026-10-12; current SQLite release separately identified as 3.54.0 (S04).
sources.locator: Overview; How WAL Works; Concurrency; Performance Considerations; The WAL File; The WAL-Reset Bug (§11).
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official SQLite WAL documentation and inspected the captured sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL allows readers and a writer concurrently but only one writer per file; all database processes must be on the same host because the wal-index uses shared memory; checkpointing is automatic by default around 1000 pages but long readers can prevent completion; the WAL file is persistent database state and must accompany the main file; WAL durability depends on synchronous settings. The WAL-reset corruption race applied through SQLite 3.51.2 and is fixed in 3.51.3 and later.
sources.applicability: Supports SQLite as a local transactional store, while ruling out a shared network-file WAL and raw main-file copying. It also yields a minimum version-history check for any WAL candidate.
sources.critic_observed_operation: Opened WAL page; examined concurrency, checkpoint, WAL-file state, same-host constraint and WAL-reset/version conditions.

reviser_independent_recheck.observed_operation: Reopened official SQLite WAL page and read §§2.2, 4, and 6 on reader end marks, checkpoint progress/starvation, one-writer concurrency, and live WAL persistent state.
reviser_independent_recheck.condition: A reader pins an end mark during its transaction; checkpoints stop at pages beyond active readers. Persistent starvation requires continuously overlapping readers/no reader gap. The WAL file contains persistent DB state; only-one-host WAL constraint remains applicable.
reviser_independent_recheck.applicability: SCW-01 live main-file-only copy hazard; SCW-06 reader duration and persistent checkpoint starvation. Does not establish all closed-copy or platform durability guarantees.

sources.title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
sources.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned official documentation; applicable mechanics reopened with SQLite 3.54.0 documentation set.
sources.locator: Introduction; Hardware Assumptions; Testing Atomic Commit Behavior (§8).
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official atomic-commit article.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Atomicity means all changes in one database transaction happen or none do, including interrupted commits under stated filesystem/OS assumptions. The detailed single-file rollback-journal walkthrough is explicitly for rollback mode; WAL uses a different mechanism. Crash tests simulate filesystem/power-loss damage and verify all-or-nothing transaction recovery and integrity.
sources.applicability: Supports one-laptop save atomicity as a primitive. It does not merge laptop histories or establish photo-file/database cross-resource atomicity.
sources.critic_observed_operation: Opened atomic commit article; confirmed one-transaction scope and rollback-mode mechanics caveat.

sources.title: SQLite Online Backup API
sources.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned official documentation reopened 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Using the SQLite Online Backup API (§1); Other Backup Techniques (§1.1); Online Backup of a Running Database (§3).
sources.observed_operation: Opened the backup documentation and read the snapshot, copy, and error-handling conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A completed online backup is a bitwise-identical snapshot from the start of the operation. Incremental backup allows writers between reads; concurrent source writes may cause restart, and continuous restarts can prevent completion. Direct external copy can block writers or leave a corrupted destination after power/OS failure.
sources.applicability: A database-aware backup can support coherent manual transfer of a snapshot. It is not by itself a change merge or a replacement for an import receipt.
sources.critic_observed_operation: Opened Backup API page; confirmed snapshot and backup-method scope.

reviser_independent_recheck.observed_operation: Reopened official SQLite Backup API page §§1 and 3; read direct external-copy limitations and completed online-backup snapshot behavior.
reviser_independent_recheck.condition: An external file copy may leave a corrupted destination after power/OS failure during copy. A completed online backup is a source snapshot; concurrent writes can restart an incremental backup.
reviser_independent_recheck.applicability: SCW-01: supports recommending a database-aware snapshot and copy verification, but does not prove that every closed/checkpointed copy is unsafe.

sources.title: CouchDB Replication and Conflict Model
sources.released_version_or_commit: Apache CouchDB 3.5 stable documentation line; official stable PDF export reported Release 3.5.2 at access. Exact patch build of the page is not exposed.
sources.locator: Replication and conflict model; Revision tree; Working with conflicting documents; compaction/pruning discussion.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official CouchDB conflict documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Revision branches retain concurrent leaves; a deterministic winner is shown by ordinary GET; clients must request conflicts/open revisions to inspect all tips. Conflict resolution explicitly updates one branch and deletes other leaf revisions. Compaction discards non-leaf bodies but retains revision identifiers, subject to revision pruning.
sources.applicability: Candidate replication model and warning that winner display, complete human history, and field-level merges require application code.
sources.critic_observed_operation: Opened CouchDB conflict docs; inspected ordinary GET, deterministic winner, conflict request and revision-tree/compaction context.

reviser_independent_recheck.observed_operation: Reopened CouchDB 3.5 stable conflict guide §§2.3.3–2.3.4; inspected ordinary GET, ?conflicts=true, open_revs=all, and revision fetch behavior.
reviser_independent_recheck.condition: Basic GET returns only the deterministic winner without indicating hidden conflicts; conflict options expose other revision IDs and callers fetch leaves. Compaction drops non-leaf bodies and revision pruning exists.
reviser_independent_recheck.applicability: SCW-03: ordinary reads can conceal alternatives; a review UI must explicitly retrieve branches. Candidate library behavior is not product policy.

sources.title: CouchDB Replication Introduction
sources.released_version_or_commit: Apache CouchDB 3.5 stable documentation line; exact stable patch not exposed on page.
sources.locator: Replication aim/procedure; deletion as revision; deleted-document filter note; PouchDB offline-client note.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official replication documentation and read deletion/filter conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Replication aims to copy active documents and propagate source deletions when documents are deleted through tombstone revisions. Content-dependent replication filters may not receive deleted content; a special _deleted:true field preserves content for filter evaluation but also retains record data and attachments. PouchDB implements the CouchDB replication algorithm for offline client use.
sources.applicability: Supports an offline replication alternative while informing delete, tombstone-retention, and photo-privacy design.
sources.critic_observed_operation: Opened CouchDB replication intro; inspected deletion revision, content-dependent filter condition, and deleted-content workaround.

reviser_independent_recheck.observed_operation: Reopened CouchDB 3.5 stable Replication Introduction §§2.1.3–2.1.5; inspected deletion-revision propagation and filter conditions.
reviser_independent_recheck.condition: Deletion is represented as a new revision and propagated to target. Only content-dependent filters may lack old document content for a deleted revision; the _deleted:true workaround retains data and attachments.
reviser_independent_recheck.applicability: SCW-02: condition must remain scoped to content-dependent filters; ordinary unfiltered tombstone propagation is separately documented.

sources.title: CouchDB Document Attachments API
sources.released_version_or_commit: Apache CouchDB 3.5 stable documentation line; exact stable patch not exposed on page.
sources.locator: §1.4.1.1 Attachments.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official document API and inspected attachment metadata and data-return parameters.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Normal document responses expose attachment metadata, not the bytes. Attachment data is returned only when requested via attachments=true or related options; attachment metadata includes digest and MIME type.
sources.applicability: Shows that metadata-only exchange can be possible by request choice, but does not establish that every replication mode will avoid byte transfer. Validate the selected Couch/Pouch path.
sources.critic_observed_operation: Opened CouchDB attachment API; inspected metadata and explicit attachments=true byte retrieval.

sources.title: PouchDB Replication Guide
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current moving official guide; not version-pinned. See S21 for the separately recorded official release listing.
sources.locator: CouchDB sync; setup; live replication/retry; deleting replicated databases.
sources.observed_operation: Opened PouchDB's official guide and inspected sample local-to-remote sync and restart/deletion behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A local PouchDB may sync to a CouchDB endpoint; live sync can stop on connectivity error unless retry is enabled. Replication tracks database contents, so destroying a replicated database can cause contents to be transferred again; document removal/tombstones are distinct.
sources.applicability: Candidate integration and explicit offline/reconnect behavior; does not establish that hosted service or credentials are required.
sources.critic_observed_operation: Opened PouchDB replication guide; inspected local/remote options, retry condition, and destroy versus remove.

sources.title: PouchDB Conflict Guide
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current moving official guide; latest official release found was PouchDB 9.0.0, but guide is not version-pinned.
sources.locator: Immediate conflicts; eventual conflicts; conflict retrieval using {conflicts:true}.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official conflict guide.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Stale-revision writes can return 409; after offline peers diverge, a deterministic winner is returned while competing revision IDs remain discoverable and must be resolved by application code.
sources.applicability: Supports displaying an explicit review queue and avoiding silent reliance on the default winner.
sources.critic_observed_operation: Opened PouchDB conflict guide; inspected immediate versus offline eventual conflicts and default winner/conflict option.

reviser_independent_recheck.observed_operation: Reopened official moving PouchDB conflict guide in its Eventual conflicts section; inspected default winner and {conflicts:true}/losing-revision fetch guidance.
reviser_independent_recheck.condition: After offline peers diverge, default CouchDB-compatible replication chooses a deterministic winner; the conflicts option reports branches, and losing revisions must be fetched separately. Guide is not version-pinned.
reviser_independent_recheck.applicability: SCW-03: C is supported and C* is contradicted. Do not confuse the library default projection with human resolution.

sources.title: Automerge Conflict Semantics
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current moving official docs accessed 2026-10-12; release history page listed JS v3.4.1 as latest stable, short commit 8d7b12f. Exact docs build-to-tag mapping not exposed; Rust crate version is not inferred.
sources.locator: What is a Conflict; getConflicts; internal operation IDs and deterministic ordering.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official Automerge conflict docs.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Concurrent writes to the same property choose one deterministic visible value, retain competing values in getConflicts, and remove conflict metadata after a later assignment. Winner order uses operation counters and actor IDs, not wall-clock time.
sources.applicability: Supports CRDT candidate and shows that retaining values does not remove the need for visible human review or explicit resolution history.
sources.critic_observed_operation: Opened Automerge conflict docs; confirmed visible deterministic value, conflicts object and conflict metadata removal after assignment.

sources.title: Automerge Merge Rules
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current moving official docs; JS stable release context v3.4.1 from S16. Rust binding/API version not inferred.
sources.locator: Map merge rules and list merge rules.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official Automerge merge-rule reference.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Different map keys combine; deleting a key while another peer makes no change removes it; deleting a key while another peer sets it yields the set value; concurrent sets choose a deterministic value. Concurrent list insertions/deletions use stable element IDs.
sources.applicability: Shows why observation deletion must be modeled as an explicit conflict/tombstone and not a bare map-key deletion.
sources.critic_observed_operation: Opened Automerge merge rules; confirmed rules are scoped to nested maps/lists and concurrent map delete/set behavior.

reviser_independent_recheck.observed_operation: Reopened Automerge moving official Merge Rules page, map rules; inspected concurrent delete of key x with peer set of x.
reviser_independent_recheck.condition: For nested map keys, if A deletes x and B sets x to a new value, merged map contains B’s new value. This page describes data-structure merge rules, not observation lifecycle.
reviser_independent_recheck.applicability: SCW-05: C is supported as motivation for app-level tombstones; C* is neither specified nor contradicted for an observation-level tombstone.

sources.title: RFC 9562: Universally Unique Identifiers
sources.locator: §5.4 UUIDv4; §5.7 UUIDv7; §6.9 uniqueness.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the RFC Editor's standards document.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: UUIDv4 uses random or pseudorandom bits for identity. UUIDv7 embeds Unix-epoch milliseconds plus random/counter fields, so time is in the identifier and should not be treated as causal proof.
sources.applicability: Supports globally unique observation/change/device identifiers while preserving the brief's ban on wall-clock conflict ordering.
sources.critic_observed_operation: Opened RFC 9562; confirmed UUIDv4 random fields and UUIDv7 timestamp field; did not treat uniqueness as absolute.
